title: Graphic update to my Valheim-like mobile game (WIP)
author: nospoon99
selftext:
For this project I really wanted to focus on gameplay and progression first but now that I'm in a good place I spent some time on the graphical side.

I feel like this is decent progress. Better shaders and lighting goes a long way.

**Method:** I used the reference image method: generate goal images with ChatGPT, then write a prompt including the /goal command to ensure Claude keep iterating (gauntlet loop should work too). My goal here wasn't to match the images exactly but rather to get 60-70% there. 

It did struggle with some assets like the heathers. I realised later my Blender MCP wasn't connected so it was all CLI. After the run, I connected Blender, got Claude on the task to create the heathers only and results for this specific asset was much better.

I purposefully went look first, optimisation second. So unsurprisingly the end result wasn't well optimised. On my old phone, it would struggle to run at 60 fps and it would get hot quickly.

I then did a bunch of optimisation: a bit of trial and error, looking up the best practices and techniques, then implement and run benchmarks. A lot of efforts went on optimising the grass / flower elements.

I also realised it's quite common to offer a 30fps / 60fps setting for phone games so I added that and sure enough battery + heat at 30fps is really good now.

Gameplay is also progressing, still 3-4h playable but more polished after following feedback from early play testers.

\> Looking for more internal testers on Google Play. If anyone is interested hit me up.

As before, tools used:  
\- Opus 5.5

\- Godot MCP with C#

\- Blender MCP

\- Reference image from ChatGPT image 2.5

replies.author: nospoon99
replies.body: I guess you mean Valheim like? It's the main inspiration for the game really, especially in terms of building (free building) and progression.

replies.author: Csilo
replies.body: Yeah my bad but the point stand still. Whats valheim about it? You could call it minecraft like atp? Its just a survival game there's nothing that makes me think of Valheim about this.

replies.author: nospoon99
replies.body: I get what you mean and from the video you're definitely not going to see what's Valheim about it, so it's my bad for leading with that. So what's similar : the open biome system, with steep progression. The building system with planks, angled roofs, stairs etc..  and free placement (not blocks like Minecraft or pre made buildings). Important food system, similar ish crafting. The difference : it's a mobile game first, so more permissive, less grindy. Basically increase the cosyness and reduce the grind. And biggest difference will be the fighting system which I want more dynamic and again mobile friendly. I won't be as complex as well, I expect there are a lot of details I'll leave out especially at the beginning (like farming)

replies.author: Csilo
replies.body: On paper the first half looked interesting. But then you started describing how you butchered the Valheim gameplay loop to resort to yet another cozy survival with nothing original about it.

replies.author: nospoon99
replies.body: Genuinely interesting to hear your take, thank you. I'm still hesitant about some key gameplay elements so I'll think about it. Maybe a better balance it to keep the game's exigence but add the quality of life elements missing in Valheim (probably the biggest critic I see about it )
